title: Grateful Dead Live at The Omni on 1991-04-05
lineage: Master Cassettes (Maxell MX-S 90) Tascam 112MKII -> Korg MR-1, 1bit 2.8MHz -> USB -> Korg Audio Gate Software 24bit 48KHz -> Wave Lab 6.0 w/UAD -> R8brain for 16bit 44.1KHz sample rate conversion -> Traders Little Helper flac8 -> Tag With Tag & Rename
source: Front Row OTS, Nakamichi CM-300 w/CP-4 shotgun caps -> Sony TC-D5M

ai_review.summary: Near‑perfect sound with a slight Dolby‑induced high‑end dullness, and a well‑played first set (though the Friend of the Devil feels odd).
ai_review.review: The recording is generally clear and balanced, but one reviewer notes that the heavy Dolby processing mutes some high frequencies. Musically the first set is praised as solid, while the rendition of "Friend of the Devil" with Bruce on keys is described as unusual. Overall the show is enjoyable despite the minor tonal coloration.

ai_rating.rationale: Both reviewers commend the performance and overall sound, but one points out a noticeable Dolby‑related high‑end loss, giving a balanced yet largely positive assessment.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Sound is near perfect; however, excessive Dolby processing results in a swallowed high‑end and a slightly compressed feel.

show_quality.setlist_flow: First set described as well played; overall pacing is solid with no major issues noted beyond the odd version of "Friend of the Devil".

band_member_comments.Keys: Bruce's playing on "Friend of the Devil" is noted as odd, suggesting an atypical keyboard approach for that song.
